matches.assumption: the laws that define a function can always be run as tests; shown false if a definition's postconditions cannot be turned into an executable check
matches.change: adds that defining a function at its type and writing its test are one act, so definition yields verification with no separate step

matches.assumption: every named type is a subtype carved by a predicate, so type, constructor and forget always derive from one predicate; false if a useful type has no predicate behind it
holding code as an ordinary datum buys the meta-recursion the interpreter-in-Luthier needs more than it costs in complexity; false if the kernel cannot reduce terms given as data cheaply

the language a program speaks is fixed by which forgetful functor it applies, so forgetting is a first-class choice; false if controlling forgetting turns out not to tame the growth of accumulated typing
all of Luthier's execution can be cast as verifying equivalences of expressions; false if some needed computation has no reading as an equivalence check
each discipline's content reduces to invariances a language can carry; false if a discipline's useful structure is not an invariance
matches.change: lifts the invariant from one concept's type to the stated aim of the whole language: to express the invariances of each discipline

matches.assumption: many equivalent implementation paths can be proven equivalent and ranked by estimated cost, so declaration and optimization can be one tool; false if proving path equivalence stays intractable (its lineage calls it the hardest part)

a bodyless typed declaration can serve all five roles with 'do not execute until defined' as its only semantics, needing no External type or core symbol; false if any of the five roles demands its own construct
Curry-Howard holds throughout Luthier so a term is a proof of its type; false if a useful type admits terms that are not proofs of the proposition it stands for
a small set of hand-executable founding components can generate the whole edifice of concepts; false if some needed concept cannot be built from them and must be native
